original_question: For a finite group G of odd order, is the maximal symmetry number always strictly larger than 1/r^2 for every r > 1?
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right object and the right inequality: it targets finite groups of odd order, asks for a strict lower bound rather than a weak one, and uses the threshold 1/r^2 that is central to the paper’s Section 7 discussion. It is also aimed at the non-Abelian extension of the preceding Abelian odd-order result.
missing_details: In the paper, the quantity is the r-th maximal symmetry number ms_r(G), not an unqualified 'maximal symmetry number'; it depends on the number of colors r.
The variable r is a positive integer (equivalently, a finite number of colors), typically written r > 1 or r >= 2 in context, not an arbitrary real parameter.
The group is considered with the normalized Haar measure; for a finite group this is the uniform probability measure, so ms_r(G) is a proportion of |G| rather than an absolute cardinality.
The relevant symmetries are the central symmetries s_c(x) = c x^{-1} c, not arbitrary automorphisms or arbitrary symmetries.

To be stand-alone, the question should define ms_r(G): it is the largest alpha such that every r-coloring of G contains a monochromatic subset A symmetric with respect to some central symmetry and having |A| >= alpha|G|.

The paper’s nearby context matters: Theorem 7.5 gives only the weak bound ms_r(G) >= 1/r^2 for odd-order finite groups, while Theorem 7.6 proves the strict bound only for finite Abelian groups of odd order; Question 7.7 asks whether that strict inequality extends to all odd-order groups.
refined_question: Let G be a finite group of odd order. For an integer r >= 2, let ms_r(G) denote the maximal symmetry number of G with respect to the family of central symmetries s_c(x) = c x^{-1} c; equivalently, ms_r(G) is the largest real number alpha such that every r-coloring of G contains a monochromatic subset A with A = c A^{-1} c for some c in G and |A| >= alpha|G|. Is it true that ms_r(G) > 1/r^2 for every finite group G of odd order and every integer r >= 2?
justification: The draft is trying to capture Question 7.7, not a broader neighboring problem. Section 7 first fixes the symmetry notion on compact groups by taking central symmetries s_c(x) = c x^{-1} c and defines ms_r(G) as the r-color maximal symmetry number for the corresponding symmetry measure space. In the finite-group part of Section 7, Theorem 7.5 gives the general lower bound ms_r(G) >= 1/r^2 when |G| is odd, and Theorem 7.6 strengthens this to the strict inequality ms_r(G) > 1/r^2 for finite Abelian groups of odd order. The paper then asks exactly whether that strict inequality remains true for every odd-order group in Question 7.7. So the refined question should keep the scope narrow: finite odd-order groups, the central-symmetry maximal symmetry number ms_r(G), and the strict bound 1/r^2, with r interpreted as the finite number of colors.
